original_question: More generally, how can one determine the autoparallel submanifolds of a Riemannian manifold endowed with a connection whose dual connection is flat?
target_in_paper: Section 6, item 2 (Hiroshi Nagaoka): the general-form open problem stated immediately after the quantum density-operator version, asking for the determination of autoparallel submanifolds for a connection whose dual connection is flat. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual wording: it captures the 'more general form' of the problem, keeps the focus on autoparallel submanifolds, and preserves the key dual-flatness hypothesis rather than drifting to a broader neighboring question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
missing_details: The Riemannian metric should be explicit, because the paper's dual (conjugate) connection is metric-dependent: in Section 5, item 2, Equation (2), the dual connection is defined relative to a Riemannian metric and an affine connection. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The question should specify which connection defines autoparallelity: it is the given affine connection ∇ whose dual connection ∇* is flat, not the Levi-Civita connection or an unspecified connection. This is implicit in the Section 6 statement. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

To be fully stand-alone, 'autoparallel submanifold' should be defined, e.g. a submanifold N ⊂ M such that ∇_X Y is tangent to N for all vector fields X,Y tangent to N. The paper uses this notion but does not restate the definition in the general-form sentence. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The paper presents the general problem as arising from a more specific quantum problem on the manifold of strictly positive density operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, viewed as a search for quantum analogues of exponential families; that contextual motivation is part of the nearby intent. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

A faithful stand-alone rewrite should not silently add extra hypotheses not stated in the paper's general form, such as completeness, compactness, torsion-freeness of the given connection, or an already-specified classification procedure. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

No ambient ring/field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifier such as 'for all sufficiently large m' belongs to this problem; introducing such algebraic restrictions would depart from the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
refined_question: Given a Riemannian manifold (M,g) and an affine connection ∇ on M, let ∇* be the g-dual connection, defined by X[g(Y,Z)] = g(∇_X Y, Z) + g(Y, ∇*_X Z) for all vector fields X, Y, Z on M. Assuming that ∇* is flat, determine the ∇-autoparallel submanifolds of M; that is, determine all submanifolds N ⊂ M such that ∇_X Y is tangent to N whenever X and Y are tangent vector fields on N. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
justification: Section 6, item 2 gives this as the paper's explicit 'more general form' of the preceding quantum autoparallelity problem, while Section 5, item 2 supplies the only nearby formal definition needed to make the statement self-contained, namely the definition of the dual/conjugate connection. The rewrite therefore stays at the paper's exact level of generality, clarifies the metric dependence of duality, makes explicit which connection defines autoparallelity, and avoids importing restrictions the paper does not state. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
